skills.name: RapidProcessResponse
skills.initiation: An assigned host has a newly flagged process PID or observed user compromise that has not yet received a response for this evidence version.
policy: Read the host-specific open case, flagged PID, evidence age, and prior outcomes; never confuse a peer's alert with local proof.
For a freshly Monitor-flagged local PID, promptly Remove on that exact host rather than first spending another Analyse turn merely to rediscover the same warning.

A TRUE Remove result only certifies completion. When available, review the case and Analyse once to check privilege escalation or remaining indicators; use PrivilegedRecovery if admin indicators are observed.
Do not Remove again on the same historical file alone. Wait automatically during IN_PROGRESS; make a fresh decision as soon as completion is observable.
skills.termination: The flagged evidence has received a response and its follow-up has been reviewed, or privileged recovery is needed.

skills.name: EscalationDiagnosis
skills.initiation: A completed Remove needs follow-up, or an unresolved local case has new evidence that has not been analysed and cannot yet justify a specific response.
policy: Select the exact open-case host needing diagnosis, including earlier alerts retained while another action was busy.
Analyse once for the pending evidence version and inspect the returned file indicators after completion.
Observed escalate.sh/escalate.exe justifies Restore; observed cmd.sh/cmd.exe before any response justifies Remove. A repeated old cmd file after Remove alone does not prove a fresh attacker session.
Do not repeat Analyse on an unchanged, already reviewed evidence version. Stop when the result has been consumed and the next response or quiet observation is appropriate.
skills.termination: The analysis result is reviewed, a response is indicated, or analysis failed and requires reassessment.

skills.name: PrivilegedRecovery
skills.initiation: An unresolved assigned-host case contains observed admin privilege-escalation file indicators and no later successful Restore for that evidence.
policy: Identify the exact host with observed escalate.sh/escalate.exe; peer severity or ordinary connection INFO alone is insufficient.
Restore that host promptly. Remove cannot terminate privileged root/SYSTEM persistence; repeated Analyse cannot repair it.
Account for the Restore availability cost, but do not indefinitely defer recovery of confirmed admin compromise solely because recovery is disruptive.
Wait for completion and inspect TRUE/FALSE. A successful Restore completes this workflow; only new observed evidence reopens it.
skills.termination: Restore completed and its status was read, or recovery failed and requires reassessment.

skills.name: SelectiveDeception
skills.initiation: There is no outstanding local compromise response or verification, and a valid assigned host without an already successful own decoy is useful for one deliberate deployment.
policy: Prioritize open local threat cases over discretionary deception; select an exact assigned host only after reading the case ledger.
DeployDecoy once on a suitable host lacking a recorded successful own deployment. Do not spread or repeat decoys simply to remain active.
Use the returned deployment status to verify execution; do not Analyse merely to prove that a completed decoy exists.
After success stop. Reattempt a failure only after its observed cause or relevant evidence changes; quiet Sleep is a valid choice.
skills.termination: Deployment completed or failed and its status has been inspected, or an urgent threat case needs attention.

skills.name: NetworkContainment
skills.initiation: Observed threat-origin bits or confirmed local compromise support a specific cross-zone containment decision; the peer busy bit alone is not a threat.
policy: Read the explicitly decoded peer identities and threat-origin bits, current mission phase, and local case evidence.
Use BlockTrafficZone only for a justified, exact destination subnet. Preserve availability by avoiding broad repeated blocks without new evidence.
Record the actual result, stop after reassessing it, and leave recovery to a later evidence-based decision.
skills.termination: The targeted block result has been reviewed or the observable containment trigger no longer applies.

skills.name: TrafficRecovery
skills.initiation: A successful own BlockTrafficZone is recorded and current observations support reassessing its availability cost.
policy: Use only an exact subnet in own_observed_blocks; do not invent another defender's block.
Check current local cases and decoded peer threat reports, then AllowTrafficZone when the earlier containment is no longer justified.
Inspect completion and stop. Never repeatedly toggle the same subnet without a changed observed reason.
skills.termination: Traffic recovery completed or failed and the result was reviewed.

skills.name: SelectiveDeception_v2
skills.initiation: IF there is an open local threat case OR a valid assigned host without a successful decoy deployment AND no outstanding local compromise response OR verification is pending
policy: Prioritize hosts with flagged PIDs or suspicious file indicators over discretionary deception; select an exact assigned host only after reviewing the case ledger and threat indicators.
DeployDecoy once on the first suitable host lacking a recorded successful deployment; avoid unnecessary repetition or spreading of decoys unless new threat indicators are observed.
Verify the deployment status immediately after execution; terminate if successful, or reattempt only after identifying the cause of failure or observing new evidence.
skills.termination: Stop IF the decoy deployment has been verified as successful OR failed with clear status inspection OR an urgent threat case requires immediate attention

skills.name: TrafficRecovery_v2
skills.initiation: IF a successful BlockTrafficZone is recorded AND there is clear, recent evidence that the containment is no longer justified
policy: Verify that the BlockTrafficZone was successful and that the containment rationale is no longer valid based on current observations and peer threat reports.
Confirm that the subnet in question is part of own_observed_blocks and has not been manually reassigned or modified by another system.
AllowTrafficZone only after a thorough reassessment of the threat landscape and peer observations, ensuring that the decision is justified by updated evidence.
skills.termination: Stop IF the traffic recovery has been fully executed, the outcome has been reviewed, and there is no indication of renewed threats or need for recontainment.

skills.name: RapidProcessResponse_v2
skills.initiation: IF a new flagged process PID is detected on a host AND the evidence has not been reviewed AND the current state of the PID is confirmed active
policy: Step 1: Validate the flagged PID's current activity and ensure it is not a false positive or unrelated to the host's security state.
Step 2: Immediately initiate a Remove action on the flagged PID without prior analysis unless the PID's activity is inconclusive or privileged access is suspected.
Step 3: After a TRUE Remove, systematically review the host for privilege escalation indicators or remaining artifacts, and apply PrivilegedRecovery if admin-level threats are confirmed.
skills.termination: Stop IF the flagged evidence has received a confirmed response, all follow-up analysis is complete, and no remaining indicators of compromise are present.

skills.name: EscalationDiagnosis_v2
skills.initiation: IF a completed Remove action requires follow-up OR new, unresolved evidence is detected, AND the evidence version has changed OR a new alert is present
policy: Step 1: Verify the evidence version and file indicators before initiating analysis; only proceed if new evidence or a change in status is detected.
Step 2: Analyse the pending evidence version and inspect returned file indicators to determine if a response (Restore or Remove) is justified.
Step 3: If old cmd files persist after a successful Remove, evaluate whether they are artifacts or indicative of a fresh session; do not re-analyse unchanged evidence.
skills.termination: Stop IF the analysis result is reviewed, a response is indicated, or the evidence version remains unchanged and no new insights are gained.

skills.name: PrivilegedRecovery_v2
skills.initiation: IF the host contains active admin privilege escalation indicators (e.g., escalate.sh/escalate.exe) AND the host has not been successfully cleaned or analyzed AND the host is not in a state that precludes restoration
policy: Confirm the host is in a compromised state with active privilege escalation indicators and not already cleaned or analyzed.
Initiate immediate Restore action on the confirmed compromised host, bypassing unnecessary delays or 'Sleep' actions.
Verify the presence of persistent escalation indicators (e.g., escalate.sh/escalate.exe) before and after Restore to ensure effectiveness.
Monitor the Restore outcome in real-time and do not terminate until the host is confirmed secure or further recovery is required.
skills.termination: Stop IF the Restore status is confirmed as successful and the host is no longer in a compromised state, or if the host requires no further recovery actions.

skills.name: SelectiveDeception_v2_c1
skills.initiation: IF there is an open threat case OR flagged PID activity AND there is a valid assigned host without a recorded successful decoy deployment
policy: Prioritize threat cases over discretionary deception; only initiate on hosts without prior successful decoy deployments.
DeployDecoy once on a suitable host with no prior successful deployment; avoid repeating or spreading decoys without verification.
Immediately verify deployment status upon completion; stop after success or after analyzing failure cause; avoid redundant Sleep actions.
skills.termination: Stop IF deployment status has been verified OR an urgent threat case requires immediate attention OR no further valid hosts remain for deployment.

skills.name: NetworkContainment_v2
skills.initiation: IF threat-origin bits are observed OR local compromise is confirmed OR flagged PIDs are present, AND mission phase aligns with active threat response
policy: Evaluate peer identities, threat-origin bits, mission phase, and local case evidence to determine threat context.
Apply BlockTrafficZone only on exact, justified destination subnets, prioritizing containment over passive observation.
Record the outcome, reassess the threat context, and do not terminate until evidence-based recovery or containment is confirmed.
skills.termination: Stop IF the block result has been reviewed, containment strategy is executed, or the threat context no longer supports containment actions.

skills.name: SelectiveDeception_v3
skills.initiation: IF there is an open local threat case OR a valid assigned host without a successful decoy deployment AND no outstanding local compromise response OR verification is pending AND flagged PID or suspicious file indicators are present
policy: Prioritize hosts with flagged PIDs or suspicious file indicators over discretionary deception; select an exact assigned host only after reviewing the case ledger and threat indicators.
DeployDecoy once on the first suitable host lacking a recorded successful deployment; avoid unnecessary repetition or spreading of decoys unless new threat indicators are observed.
Verify the deployment status immediately after execution; terminate if successful, or reattempt only after identifying the cause of failure or observing new evidence.
skills.termination: Stop IF the decoy deployment has been verified as successful OR failed with clear status inspection OR an urgent threat case requires immediate attention OR the host already has a successful decoy deployment and no new threat indicators are present
